close_reason: Decomposed and fully implemented across four children .3.1–.3.4 — all RFC 8620 §5.4 machinery now lives in handle_task_copy: same-account rejection, fromAccountNotFound, ifFromInState/ifInState, source-id semantics (fetch from source + merge overrides + create), onSuccessDestroyOriginal + destroyFromIfInState implicit Task/set. Bespoke TasksBackend::copy_task trait method dropped in favor of the canonical-template get_objects+create_object pattern from calendars-server. All children green and merged; workspace tests 2189 passing.
description:
handle_task_copy in task.rs:400-506 omits several RFC 8620 §5.4 MUST/SHOULD requirements:

1. SAME-ACCOUNT REJECTION: §5.4 'accountId MUST be different to the fromAccountId'. The handler does not check this. A request where fromAccountId == accountId is silently accepted; the backend's copy_task is called and creates a duplicate within the same account. Per spec, this should be rejected.

2. ifFromInState / ifInState: §5.4 lists both as optional but well-defined arguments. The handler reads neither; a client passing 'ifInState' (matching the destination account's Task state) gets that argument silently dropped. State-mismatch protection is unavailable for Task/copy.

3. SOURCE-ID SEMANTICS: §5.4 'The Foo object MUST contain an id property, which is the id (in the fromAccount) of the record to be copied'. The handler at task.rs:432-439 sets a 'placeholder' id when the client omitted one — silently masking what the spec treats as a hard requirement — and then deserializes-to-Task. The id is supposed to *select what to copy from the source*; it is never passed to the backend as a 'source id' parameter. MemoryBackend.copy_task uses only the (already-deserialized) Task value the client supplied as the request payload; it never reads from from_account_id at all. Net effect: Task/copy at the kit's reference level is functionally identical to Task/set create against to_account_id, but the wire shape pretends to be a copy. A consumer with a real backend has no API surface to do the spec-mandated three-phase read.

4. onSuccessDestroyOriginal / destroyFromIfInState: §5.4 specifies that when true the server MUST emit a follow-up Task/set call against fromAccountId. Neither argument is parsed; the implicit-second-call behaviour is absent. The handler returns 'vec![]' as Invocations even when the spec mandates a synthesized destroy-of-original.

5. PER-ITEM ERRORS: §5.4 lists specific notCreated SetError types (alreadyExists, fromAccountNotFound, etc.). The handler maps via set_error_value but no code path emits 'fromAccountNotFound' specifically.

Recommended scope: file as a parent epic. Same-account rejection (#1) is the smallest-fix-largest-correctness-win item and can land alone. The source-id semantics (#3) requires reshaping copy_task's trait signature to take a source Id and a partial-overrides PatchObject, which is a larger redesign also touching every other extension server's analog. ifFromInState/ifInState (#2) is a localized add. onSuccessDestroyOriginal (#4) is foundation-level: the implicit second-call dance touches Dispatcher and likely belongs higher up — file a separate workspace-wide bead.
title: Task/copy handler is missing RFC 8620 §5.4 mandatory machinery
